stops.note: the Berwickshire town that gave the Franciscan philosopher John Duns Scotus (c. 1266-1308) his name
Duns Scotus's subtle theology dominated the schools of Oxford and Paris, and his followers were called 'Dunsmen'
Renaissance humanists and reformers mocked Scotists as hair-splitters, and 'dunce' sank to 'dullard'; the dunce's cap appears in Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop (1840)

current_meaning: a person who is slow at learning
